utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, has the individual 543 KK3 been identified as Mesa Efendic in the ICMP data base?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he has been.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And being an experienced investigator, are you satisfied that the information on which you updated the status of Mesa Efendic in the book was accurate and reliable?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I move to admit this photograph as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 06362 receives number P1530, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'd like to continue with, very briefly, with the following document. We'd have to do this I think in -- I'd like to upload 65 ter 28976. This shouldn't be broadcast. And I think we should do it in private session as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore the Prosecution -- the photo book, Muslim photo book, is tendered. Madam Registrar, is number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It was 65 ter number 28975.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And it receives number P1532, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1532 is admitted into evidence. No need to have it under seal, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I put on the record that in private session, the Defence already expressed that they had no objection to the admission of P1532.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That concludes my direct examination. Thank you very much, Ms. Gallagher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. Mr. Ivetic, we have 10 minutes left until the break. I leave it up to you, whether you consider it useful to already have those first 10 minutes or otherwise take an early break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let with check with my client and see what he would prefer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think we should take the break early and then I will I believe conclude my cross within the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take the break. Ms. Gallagher, you can follow the usher. We would like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at 20 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could Ms. Gallagher be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Ivetic is member of the defence team of Mr. Mladic. Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, Ms. Gallagher.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As was the case last time that we had occasion to hear your testimony in this courtroom, I would like to remind you that since we both speak English we should be mindful to maintain a pause between answer and question to permit the court reporters and translators to do their job. Is that fair, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to first talk about some of these AID statements that you have talked about during your direct examination and on the exhibit list now we have a number of them, I believe ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can call up, and perhaps not broadcast it just to be on the safe side, Exhibit P1523 as an example of one of these.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And while we wait for that to come up in e-court, madam, can I ask you that as a result of your investigative work, can you confirm that the AID agency for investigation and documentation was in fact staffed by the former secret police of the army of BiH side?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to be cautious in saying I don't know who the individuals are that were a part of the AID, if they were all secret, if there's a combination of civilian police. I would defer probably to Pasaga Mesic's testimony regarding the -- those that took the statements but -- so I just want to be a little cautious with my response on that because I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fair enough. Now, if we look at these statements and we now have an example on the screen although it is not being broadcast, I'd like to see what you do know about how they were taken. First of all, did you or anyone else in the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal perform any research or investigation to ascertain the precise procedure employed by those taking these statements given to the agency for investigation and documentation, the AID?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My knowledge of the process is what was stated in the testimony of Pasaga Mesic and several of the other investigators such as Dean Manning who took statements in the year 2000 as to the process. It is basically explained in his testimony and you'll see in some of these statements of what the process was, but beyond that, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, madam. Now, if we look at this document that we have on the screen, it's dated the 25th of January, 1996, and it records that this particular witness was shown a collection of -- or an album, I should say, of 29 photographs that were part of the identification process. Now, you've mentioned the testimony of Mr. Pasaga Mesic. He mentions 30 photographs. I haven't done the statistics but if you go through all of these AID statements I think you will find that whereas a large number of them refer to 29 photographs being shown, others refer to a collection of 30 photographs being shown. Do you know what is the reason for this apparent discrepancy in the number of photographs which comprise the album which was shown to these people by the AID officials in Tuzla for purposes of identification?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know -- I don't know the reason for the difference of one photograph. I might want to take a look at the exact dates of the interviews to see if 29 corresponds with one date versus 30 with another date, if perhaps there was an additional identification made or -- excuse me, an additional photograph that was contributed to the album. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can assist you, and this also should not be broadcast, but exhibit P1520 is -- when it comes up, I think we'll see it as dated in June of 1996 and references -- once the English comes up, I think you'll see it references a 30-photograph album being used. Does that allow you to refresh your recollection or do you stand by the previous answer as being complete?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think it corroborates what I just said, that you have a later date of June 20th, 1996, where there's now 30 photographs, whereas in January 1996, there was only 29. So it is only an assumption on my part. I don't know that there was an additional photograph that was contributed -- added to the album and therefore for these later interviews.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you say it's an assumption on your part. Do you have knowledge of any investigation or confirmation efforts undertaken by the Office of the Prosecutor to ensure that the set of photographs that was shown to the individuals giving the AID statements is the same one that is referred to in the Pasaga Mesic testimony?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I myself have looked at the -- at photographs and they're in this book as the photographs that he used when he was interviewing people for the identifications so those photographs are in here. What I don't -- what I once again don't know is off the top of my head without perhaps a little more investigation or looking more closely at the photographs what is the one that was added later for the June 20th, 1996 interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. And just to be clear, I understood your testimony to be that Mr. Pasaga Mesic was relying upon these AID statements in terms of giving his Rule 61 testimony in 1996. Am I correct in that or was he relying upon other things as well according to your information and investigation?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can certainly tell from his testimony that he's relying upon these statements because they corroborate what is said in the statements. Beyond that, I don't know what else he relied upon. I'm assuming that he had other information than just these statements but I don't -- that wouldn't be fair for me to speculate about really.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you do not know whether in fact he individually interviewed people apart from these statements which were taken by other officials?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't know how it was -- I don't know which ones he would have done, others would have done. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, if we looked at the identification book, which has now received the exhibit number P1532, I believe, and that we can have up on the screen. I think the -- we have two requests for assistance, one dated 9 March, 2002, and the other 19 September 2002, and they're at pages 74 and 80 respectively of the photo -- of the Bosnian Muslim photo identification book. Now these are the responses from the BiH authorities to the Office of the Prosecutor of the Tribunal as to requests for assistance; however, we do not have the actual text of the OTP requests themselves so as to know what the documents are in answer to. Do you know if the requests were in writing or orally submitted?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The protocol is that it's in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. I was aware of that. That's why I'm asking was it sent in writing or was it transmitted orally?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: My recollection -- well, let's put it this way: I don't recall seeing the written request, the original request. The fact that they refer to numbers and it's the practice of the office to put things in writing and the fact that it came back in writing, my assumption is that it was done in writing, but I have not seen the original request.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you at least have information as to when these original requests would have been made, perhaps the year that the requests would have been sent to the BiH authorities?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the first one, you'll see -- and this is the one that's for the year 2000, and it has a date to The Hague of March 9th, 2000 with a request number, which would be the RFA number dated 10 February 2000. So that suggests that there was a request made February 10th, 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, I see that later in that same letter, we see apparently another request dated the 15th of February, 2000.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be your assumption that there have been two requests there dated on the 10th and the 15th of February?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, the reason I ask is that the rule 61 of Pasaga Mesic that we've referred to and that's included as part of this identification book at annex 3, I believe, starting in e-court at page 37 of the same, and dated in 1996, in that transcript - and I believe at pages 39 and 40 in e-court of this book, at lines 30 and onwards on page 39 - the testimony requests that the deponent, Mr. Pasaga Mesic, does not know where the photographs came from but does testify that the investigative team of the Tribunal asked for efforts to identify the persons in the photographs. So the question that I have for you is if the photographs used in the AID statements were part of the same or prior request for assistance issued by the Office of the Prosecutor, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the photographs, these 29, 30 photographs have been the same throughout and the fact that the -- many of these names mentioned certainly correspond with the photographs in those that were identified. But otherwise -- so I'm assuming that yes, it's the same group.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But do you know where they came from? Did they come from the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, okay, I understand your question now. Yes, I believe they were photographs that were taken from that Jean-Rene Ruez had captured from the Petrovic video and the other footage that's from July 12th in Potocari. Those photographs were then given to Pasaga Mesic and his team in Tuzla, and those were the photographs that were shown to the interviewees which then are encapsulated in this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, is it your testimony that Mr. Ruez captured the Petrovic video in 1996?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would there be any written documentation required under the protocols of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal providing the photographs to the BiH authorities such that we can confirm what photographs and other information were provided to the BiH authorities that resulted in the AID statements being taken?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- generally, yes, we would know which photographs had been handed over. Sometimes it does -- sometimes it might be too many photographs that might not be documented in a request. It might happen more as it's written into the request and then the photographs are handed over personally on a separate occasion. I actually did try to find what the original photographs, if there was some sort of album that had been copied, anything here. As to what exactly what had been turned over, I wasn't able to find documentation of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would it have been standard operating procedure under the protocols in existence as you know them for such documentation to exist?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say usually but not always in that sometimes there may be -- there may be -- it may be too large, too many photographs that can be part of a -- or an official request that goes to other authorities, and it may be documented as to what is being turned over or requested of. So I don't want to say that that would be always the case, and perhaps also in 1996 when procedures were being developed, they were not set in place as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I want to move to a different topic and it starts with something you said yesterday. You testified about the accuracy of Pasaga Mesic's Rule 61 testimony and to be specific and fair, at transcript page 12.191, line 17 and onward, you testified as follows. And I'll try to read slow enough so as not to cause grief for the translators and the court reporter: "Q. And in terms of your examination as to the identity of the individuals that are named in the book, did you find any discrepancies in terms of the information you found in the evidence of Pasaga Mesic versus the information you found in the statements of various individuals that also identified the same person? "A. For -- for the most part, no. His testimony correlates with the statements that are listed in the indexes. There were a couple of minor mistakes that were made, such as a -- in his testimony, perhaps a wrong age. Or on one occasion there is one woman who is identified in the book and he had testified it was a male -- with male's name instead. But otherwise the information that he gave in his testimony is the same as the information that's in the statements." Now, the reason I have highlighted that is I'd like to turn to the book and -- so again, it's page 74 in e-court of the book, and it is the first response of the BiH authorities to the request for information to the ICTY. And if we wait for that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is the page in hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 74 in e-court. It has the ERN number ending in 076.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page, madam, there is a note that says: "This communication corrected the testimony of Pasaga Mesic regarding the missing status of Huseinovic, Ibro, and Mujcinovic Mustafa. Their status was corrected from missing to living." Does -- did this note come -- arise as a result of your investigative updating of the book or is this something that predated you?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is something from the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that these mistakes in the Mesic -- Pasaga Mesic Rule 61 testimony as to these two individuals is rather significant?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They -- they're significant in that they -- when I was referring to his testimony, it was testimony that he knew of. So I think at that time he believed Ibro Huseinovic and Mustafa Mujcinovic to have been the status that he gave them in the testimony. So yes, it later it -- in the year 2000, it was determined that those were -- one of them was an incorrect identification and the other one the person is alive and not missing. So those were -- that was incorrect information at the time that Pasaga Mesic reflected in his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you one thing. The fact that one of these persons was living, was that known at the time he gave his evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it's in the year 2000 that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That he was found.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That he was found alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore, is a qualification that that person was missing, is that wrong or is that right? Because the person was missing and later found to be alive which doesn't make him any less missing at the time when it was not yet known that he was alive.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. That's my recollection and that's what I was just trying to explain, that I don't think that he was misrepresenting the information that he knew at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd love to go through that with you step by step because I think you're wrong. But let's go through it to be fair. If we turn to the next page in e-court of this document, and if we look at the entry for Mr. Huseinovic, Ibro, and it says that he was in Potocari but he arrived on the first trucks to the free territory and he lives in a particular settlement, et cetera. Now, if we look at Exhibit P1528, an AID statement of Ibro Huseinovic, I think we'll see that in 1996, Mr. Huseinovic gave a statement to the AID which would have been available to Mr. Pasaga Mesic which indicated that he was alive. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can call up P1528.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I think you'll see if you look at the statement that the description of him being in Potocari and leaving on a truck and arriving in Kladanj correlates to the 2000 information that in fact he was alive, so would you agree with me that with respect to this individual, Pasaga Mesic ought to have had this information at the time that he gave his Rule 61 testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we're referring to the individual that was mentioned at annex 6 in the book, number 6, Ibro Huseinovic, this is an individual with a different father's name that's on the screen now. So unless we've changed topics, we're talking about different people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I do note that the father's name is different but the description is exactly the same of how he got out of the -- out of Potocari.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we ask the witness, then. Is that a typical description for one of these persons or was that something that has happened to more persons; that is, arriving on a truck to the free territory? And in the statement, Mr. Ivetic, perhaps you could help me because you pointed at --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's the part that's underlined, the fourth line from the bottom: "I threw myself onto some things inside the truck while the other woman in the truck hid me and protected me with their bodies," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now that is him being on a truck. Do we find the same details elsewhere? Because you said it is a similar description. Is it the similarity exclusively found in being in a truck travelling to Bosnian-held territory or is there more similarity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Being in Potocari having that name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Potocari, truck, and having this name. That's where we find the similarity, you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then we'll have to consider whether perhaps it's a mistake and it's the same person but that the name of the father is not recorded accurately or whether it is a different person who may have found himself in a similar situation being Potocari, on a truck, being transported to Bosnian-held territory. Is that the issue? Have I described the issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I was wondering whether the witness knew anything about that. If she does, enlighten us; if not, then I can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But we have now, I think, clearly identified what the issue is. Can you shed any light on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure. There are two Ibro Huseinovics that have different fathers, different dates of birth, and even spelling, and in fact they're both survivors. And one is a very statement of having left -- been one of the early ones to have left Potocari on one of the first trucks on the 12th. And therefore in the context of what had happened, some of the men were able to leave early and were able to get to the free territory. The other person describes sneaking onto a truck and being able to get out that way. But there are two separate Ibro Huseinovics, son of Aljo and son of Ahmo with a -- different dates of birth, one of about 51 years old and the other one would have been about 62 years old.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the fact that they survived, was that for both known at the time when the testimony was given.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of them, the Ibro Huseinovic, son of Aljo, the one that you see here obviously was a statement that came in by the Tuzla AID in 1996. And the other one, the son of Ahmo, that was taken in the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you know with respect to which of these Ibro Huseinovics a Mr. Hakija Huseinovic who gave a statement, which has an ERN number of 0085-8739, would have been related to?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hmm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at it? Because the number is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's not in e-court, Your Honours. I wasn't going to present it for the truth of matter asserted. It's something I found this morning when I was double-checking in EDS, and it is a statement of -- also given to AID in 1996 of a similar format, it's not one of the ones that was on the list for the Prosecution, and also identifies that Ibro Huseinovic was alive in 1996. Now, I don't know which one. That's why I'm asking the witness if she knows and she says she reviewed all these statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I don't know whether she knows them by number by heart. That's -- is there any way that you could if you found them this morning that you either make a copy or something like that because the Chamber, of course, must have an opportunity to verify --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can at the break have a copy printed and we can find out because I honestly don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- looking at it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of course it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- then I know it's which -- which Ibro Huseinovic it would have been. [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness is able to answer the question already, nevertheless I think the Chamber would like to have a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me just check the index in the back and that might give us some more information. It actually is -- it's not listed in the back, but I -- I would want to confirm this, but I do have a recollection of Hakija Huseinovic identifying Ibro Huseinovic and that would have been from 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And which Ibro Huseinovic would that statement be about? If you don't know, that's ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would want to confirm it but I think that you might be correct, but before I go any further, if I can take a look at the Hakija Huseinovic's statement just to make sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would be more than happy to find that and bring it in after the break. If we can move on though.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In terms of the selection of the term --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Oh, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do actually have a hard copy. We managed to print it out. So if Mr. Ivetic wants to put it to the witness or if the Chamber wants to see it we can provide that immediately rather than after the break --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That'd be great.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then could the hard copy -- could the usher assist in giving the hard copy to -- first of all to Mr. -- perhaps we could use our --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The last time we tried it didn't go quite as planned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, if you look at the document first, if you -- then at the same time if the usher could try to get the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Going. But yeah, that's hard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Surviving from his --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could just go into private session for one brief moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the interpretation, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise to the interpreters and I will try my best not to speak quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we look at again the identification book which is P1532, and if we return to page 76 of the same, it should be the second page of the 2000 response to request for assistance by the BiH authorities to the OTP of this Tribunal. And here now we have the information under number 20 for the second individual that is a correction from the Pasaga Mesic testimony, Mujcinovic, Mustafa, and we see that this person was not even in Potocari but was the result of a falsely identified photograph. Now -- now that is something that you did mention earlier. I want to ask you since here it says that the authorities of BiH will try to identify the person in the photograph by operative work, it has been some time since this 2000 request for assistance. Do you know whether they have accomplished any kind of identification so as to supplement the information that we have in this book?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of. I haven't seen any information that suggests they discovered or passed on to the OTP the identification of that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that it seems or appears that it took them four years to find out that the initial identification made of Mr. Mujcinovic was in fact falsely made?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly that's at the time that the OTP learns of the -- learns of the misidentification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now again as to the use of the term survivor for this individual. Since he never was in Potocari, would you agree that it's not entirely an accurate description of his status as being a survivor?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that he was mentioned as a survivor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I thought he was. Then we can move on. If we look at -- if we talk about this book, P1752, can you please tell us to what extent, if at all, the demographic unit of the Office of the Prosecution was involved in its creation or updating?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you said P1752. We haven't reached that number yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, that would be P1532. I can't read my own handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In relation to this book that we have in front of us, the photo -- the identification book that you worked on, can you tell us what if any role the demographics unit of the Office of the Prosecutor had in the creation of the same?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that they had any direct creation of this book, and in an indirect way some of the work on the Srebrenica missing persons list that they have helped create from information from ICRC and ICMP, that that is one more list that I relied upon when I was checking on the status of the missing men. But otherwise, I am not aware that they participated in the creation of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, I'd like to ask you if you have knowledge or at least during the time period when you were involved in working on this book, whether anyone else within the Office of the Prosecutor had a main role in the production of this book or was it you?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the book has remained basically essentially as it was originally created for the Blagojevic trial, so I think at that time it was investigators and the entire members of the team that usually were a part of creating these books. Since I assisted with updating it, it has been primarily my work in at least updating the status of the people, and I've relied upon other -- the work of others such as the work the demographics unit did in terms of their missing persons list, ICMP and my colleague, Dusan Janc as well with his report, but otherwise -- and the only other person would have been our technician who helps create these books and videos and other photo books here with the OTP, Zoran Lesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I know that this was before your time, so if you can't answer I'll understand, but you did mention that the -- it was your understanding that the entire team worked on this back in the time that it was first created by the Blagojevic trial. Would that have included, do you know, trial counsel that would have been prosecuting that case?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for sure. My assumption is these books generally are created there -- with investigators and with the prosecutors in determining what will go in it, what will stay out, the look of it, how it's presented in court. So this has been the practice of all the books that I've worked on over the years is that there is a dialogue with the prosecutors and they have input. I don't want to say -- I don't know specifically about when this was created for Blagojevic, who might have -- what that involvement would have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fair enough. Now I'd like to move to a different topic again. In this book, P1532, at page 13 of the same in e-court, we have -- and in the hard copies it's the page that's marked M7 at the bottom right to assist those of us with the hard copy. Now we do have it on the screen. Here, we have an individual identified Ramo Osmanovic and it lists the information of how he was identified. I believe that we had some testimony here a few weeks ago that this individual was a soldier, specifically a member of Ibro's Brigade in the Srebrenica armed enclave. Did your investigation discover or verify this same fact?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: True, I have read Saliha Osmanovic's statement from 2000 and I did see a portion of her testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in relation to your investigative work, what can you tell us about this Ibro's Brigade, what was the formal designation of this structure, of this formation?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of Ibro's Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah, if you know. If your investigation revealed anything.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I know -- I recall, I should say. I know virtually nothing about it. I recall more of his, in particular, Ramo's work as doing construction often times in Serbia and around the country and that was primarily his employment before and even up until the time that they fled the area. I don't recall actually anything about -- off the top of my head about Ibro's Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in this photograph, this individual does not seem to be wearing anything that could be readily identifiable as a military outfit. Did your investigation reveal if the armed forces of the Bosnian Muslim side in Srebrenica from operating in uniform or any other type of clothing during this time period?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the column that was moving through the woods that had fled the Srebrenica area. There are members of the column that were a part of the ABiH army that were wearing camouflage and had weapons and that more than two-thirds of the column were civilians, civilian clothes without any weapons. And yes, I've not had any indication that he was carrying a weapon or any -- in any sort of military garb as many of the others were not either.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I picked him because we had this independent confirmation of his status. As to the other 30, I guess, individuals that have been identified for purposes of this book, in relation to those individuals has your office undertaken any investigation to determine if these men had been members of the BiH armed forces in Srebrenica at any time prior or subsequent to the filming of these photographs?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of. Not for the purposes of this book.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for the vast, I believe, majority of the persons that are identified for purposes of this book, we do not have an independent statement or verification of how they met their fate and where they met their fate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, most of them we know -- we do have verification as to -- well, we have verification as to where their remains are found and that gives an indication of where they may have met their fate. And we do have exhumation reports, autopsy reports that -- on a number of them that also verifies how they met their fate. We do have some statements where in fact I -- there's one in particular I remember where there is one man who is at an execution site, goes to the execution site with one of the men here that originally was listed as missing, and he himself, the one giving the statement survived the execution. And in his statement, I recall that he says he assumes the other person was killed in the execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can perhaps assist you, I think it's P1519 that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we cannot broadcast that but if we can bring it up that might assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Does this appear to be the one that you were talking about, madam?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the one that I was thinking of.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And apart from this one that both you and I were able to locate, do you have knowledge of any other statements as to any of the other individuals that are identified as part of this book?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In terms of witnessing or being a part -- being there at the execution, this is -- I think this is the only one that I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to move to one other topic. First of all, as part of your -- and we can remove this from the monitor, I guess, I don't need it anymore. From your investigative work, have you gained knowledge about an incident where a group of detained Bosnian Muslim men tried to overpower the police guards that were guarding them, even taking the rifle of one guard and killing him and where another guard was injured trying to get that rifle back. Are you aware of such an instance?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of an instance at the Kravica warehouse where one Muslim man had grabbed the gun of -- it was -- had grabbed the gun and Rade Cuturic had wrestled the gun away, and shortly after that the men on that side of the warehouse that were kept there were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And was it part of your investigation that prior to the incident where the individual tried to overpower and take the gun from this person, that no one had been shot at this location?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was not a mass execution prior to this execution, not that I'm aware of, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I believe you identified the Kravica warehouse. Would that have been the agricultural warehouse?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, that's what it was used for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, could I ask one clarifying question. Mr. Ivetic asked you that prior to that incident where he grabbed the weapon, whether no one had been shot at this location. Your answer was: "There was not a mass execution prior to this execution," not that you're aware of. You're talking about a mass execution. Mr. Ivetic is asking about any killing. Do you have any recollection that perhaps an individual person held there may have been killed? Because you specifically referred to mass executions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, in terms of what I know specifically about the warehouse, I'm not aware of other executions before that one specifically at the warehouse. I know -- I've read a lot of statements of people in the area, so I have heard statements of executions happening nearby, in a field nearby, adjacent, so that's why I qualified it a little bit. But in terms of inside the warehouse, I'm not aware of anyone being killed in the warehouse until the executions started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what is the nearest by, would that be within 50 metres from the warehouse or would that be somewhere in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I recall is it would have been in the field near the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, near?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whether it's 50 metres, 100 metres, I'm not sure, but I don't mean -- I don't mean the village down the road. I mean in the nearby vicinity as well as a school in Kravica that's a little further away. I would not categorise that as being near the warehouse but the fields surrounding the warehouse. I don't know -- I'm sorry, I don't know the exact location so I don't want to say if it's 100 metres or 50 metres or 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the direct vicinity of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the general, yes. I would say in the nearby vicinity of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I want to return just for a moment to your work in updating this book and the information contained in it. You indicated that you did also use the lists or referred to the lists that the demographics unit would have had access to. Did you at any time seek assistance of anyone from the demographics unit to learn how to use or how to understand those lists or that information that they had? I understand it's a database that's at issue. Are we talking about the same thing or?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't have used it myself. It's a number of different -- basically a number of different databases that they used to pull together their lists. So I have used the list that -- their updates as to what they have put out regarding the Srebrenica missing persons, so it's their compilation list. So -- in that respect, it's -- I've used the one final list that they created.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So you used their finished product?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Perfect. That answers my question. Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ivetic. Have the questions in cross-examination triggered any need to further examine the witness, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just have a couple of questions, Mr. President. If we can take the break now, it would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How much time do you think you would need for those questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm guessing 5 or 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm also looking at the Defence, whether they would prefer -- because otherwise we would have to -- if we could finish now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber would have a preference to continue for 5 or 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My client is -- would permit to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's continue, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ms. Gallagher, you were asked just now a couple of questions about the killings that occurred at the Kravica warehouse on 13 July and in particular asked about the incident concerning an individual who burned his hands in relation to those events. I just want to clarify something with you because I think your answer to Mr. Ivetic's question wasn't clear, at least to me, and that related to whether or not there had been any executions prior to the individual whose hands were burnt in relation to the events there. In terms of the investigation that you've been involved in and your colleagues have been involved in, is there any concrete information as to whether or not the burned hands incident, I'll call it, occurred immediately prior to the executions or during the course of the executions that happened on the 13th? Do you have any concrete information either way which?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's -- there's many, many, many statements out there regarding that the incident of the burned hands happened early on. There are some that say it precipitated -- some that, yes, the executions had started, the shooting had started already. It's -- and when I mean -- I think it was just early on in the course of the execution or at the beginning. What I don't mean to say is it's at the end. But it's clear it happened sometime early on but I don't know if it was immediately -- if it was right before or right at the beginning of when it started. There's many different statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. You were also asked some questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I apologise to the Chamber, I don't have the exact page reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But you will recall being asked some questions about Ramo Osmanovic. In particular, his clothing, his attire in relation to whether or not he was a member of the Bosnian Muslim army, the ABiH army. And you were asked some questions about their attire and whether or not the individuals in the book were members of the army. In relation to that, I just want to ask you a couple of questions. As concerns the 31 individuals that are listed in the index in the book, in the circumstances or rather the photographs that are depicted in the book are any of those individuals at liberty?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Meaning that they are free and alive right now?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No. Meaning whether or not they are free and alive -- free to go in the photographs that are depicted in the book?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think that calls for a conclusion to be reached, Your Honours, perhaps even a legal one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would rephrase your question, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What is your understanding of the circumstances, in which the individuals depicted in the photograph, were, at the time that the photographs were filmed, were taken?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think it's -- it's clear in watching the video and the footage yourself as well as reading the statements that none of these men were free to go, whether that was in Potocari when they were being separated out to go on the buses or that was in Sandici meadow or when they were walking up towards Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me just ask this one or two last questions. The last question or topic is the number -- the 31 individuals that are identified in the index of the identification book, rather, is the book limited to the identification of those 31 individuals or does it concern other individuals? And the reason why I ask this is because Mr. Ivetic had asked you about an individual named Mujcinovic who is mentioned in annex 6, I believe it was, item number 20 of this annex as a person who he thought had been indicated as a survivor. As you can see from the index, which is page 5, I think, in e-court, of the book, nobody by the name of Mujcinovic is mentioned among the 31, so I was wondering whether or not the book is meant to include these other individuals or is limited only to the 31 here?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. The 31 individuals that are highlighted in the front part of the book are the ones that we know the status of, one way or the other. There are others as you see that are mentioned. We don't know the status -- even those that are mentioned as missing, we don't know the status, and if that's because they're -- we don't know. Their remains have not been found. If there's nobody in the family alive to ask about locations or their -- anything more about them. So the 31 that are highlighted are the ones that we have more concrete identifications of.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In respect of annexes 6 and 7, which refer to communications with the Bosnian authorities, one in annex 6 which concerns certain corrections and annex 7 which also contains additional information concerning the status of certain individuals, have those corrections or considerations been taken into account in this particular iteration of the book?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That's why they are not part of the 31 and it's been noted when there has been a correction made, an update made. So those are reflected, obviously, in these annexes, in this correspondence, and they are not a part of the main book.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, as the book stands now, is it accurate and reliable?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, have the questions in re-examination triggered any need for further cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They have not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Ms. Gallagher, this concludes your testimony. I have to look at the Prosecution -- it really concludes the testimony of Ms. Gallagher. Then, Ms. Gallagher, I would like to thank you for coming this short way to this courtroom several times and we thank you for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties, and by the Bench and you are therefore excused which means that you now can freely communicate again with whom ever you wish to communicate. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break of 20 minutes and we'll resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next witness the Prosecution will call is Witness RM313 if I am well informed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we also agreed I think and the Chamber approved a different procedure, Ms. Hasan, the procedure being that you would read the summary of the witness's testimony before he enters the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you have an opportunity to do so now.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon to everyone. Good afternoon, Your Honours. The witness lived in Srebrenica as a young boy. One day, when he remembers being about 7 years old, persons that the witness refers to as Chetniks wearing multi-coloured uniforms forced him and his father onto a green truck with other people. They were blindfolded and taken to a grassy area where they were shot. The witness was then taken to Zvornik hospital where he was treated for his wounds. The witness's evidence relates to the Prosecution's tendered Rule 92 bis evidence of RM247, a driver in the Zvornik Brigade who in July of 1995 was present at the Orahovac execution site. RM247 gives evidence that after the execution stopped, a Muslim boy of about 6 or 7 years old emerged from the dead bodies. A mustached Drina Corps lieutenant-colonel who was present at the execution site ordered that the boy be killed, and when no one complied, ordered that he be taken to Orahovac school. RM247 volunteered, and believing that the boy would be killed if taken to the school, took him instead to the hospital in Zvornik. That concludes the summary, Mr. President, and the witness can be called in at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we first move into closed session so that the protective measures of face distortion, voice distortion, and pseudonym will be effectively applied when the witness enters the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in closed session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness RM313, because we are not use your own name. We'll call you by this number. Before you give evidence, we would like you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we turn in open session which means the blinds are up, but still the outside world cannot see your face, cannot hear your own voice, and we will not use your own name. So even if the blinds are up, still not visible, still not audible, although the content of what you say will be known to those outside this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I hereby put on the record that the witness has already made his solemn declaration when we were still in closed session. Ms. Hasan, you'll examine the witness. Witness, you will first be examined by Ms. Hasan. You will find Ms. Hasan to your right and Ms. Hasan is counsel for the Prosecution. There she is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Hello, Witness. Thank you for coming in here today and for being with us. Are you sitting comfortably?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The headphones are okay on, you can hear everything well?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If they slip, you just have to put them a little bit -- the band a little bit higher on your head.

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: No, no, everything is all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Great. It's already been explained to you that no one sees you and your face is not seen and your name is not revealed, and we've discussed this earlier as well. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And everyone in this courtroom understands that this can be very difficult for you, so we're just going to take our time and you just let us know if you need a break. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we call up 65 ter 28937.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And just as that comes up, Witness, if there's any questions that I ask you or anyone else asks you that you don't understand, just tell us and we will try to make it a bit more clear for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if this document cannot be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay, Witness, if you just take a look at the screen that's in front of you, without saying anything out loud about what you see, can you tell us if that is your name displayed on that screen?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd offer 65 ter 28937 into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, 28937 receives number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1533, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1533 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just for a few brief moments can we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, we are now in private session which means that even what you say cannot be heard by anyone. So even the content of your testimony will not be known to anyone outside this courtroom. Ms. Hasan, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us what year you were born in?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And on the screen we just saw before us, we saw your full name, but do you have a nickname that you go by?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes, I'm called by other people Fahro.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Are you Muslim by faith?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what area you lived in when you were a young boy?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And do you remember who you lived with at that time?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: With my father.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us your father's name?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes, Mehmed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did your father also have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes, Meho.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We can go back into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, we now return in open session which means still your face cannot be seen, still no one will hear your own voice, but the content of what you say will be known to those outside this courtroom. We move back into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter 533 [sic] displayed but not broadcast for the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you repeat the correct number?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes it's 65 ter 5333 -- oh. Yes, that's correct. 5333.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise anyone in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Who do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And are you the person that's in between the man and the woman there?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd offer that into evidence, 65 ter 5333. Under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 5333 receives number P1534, Your Honours, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1534 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, I'm now going to ask you some questions about the events that happened to you when you were a young boy. So let's begin. Do you recall the day that you were put on a truck? Do you remember that day?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately how old you were at that time?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Seven.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And when the truck arrived at your -- sorry, when the truck arrived, where were you?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you please repeat the question? I didn't understand it completely.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Where were you when the truck came?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: At home.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And who was with you at home? Were you alone or was someone else there?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: My father was with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And can you tell us a little bit about what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: My father and I were in the house. My father was changing a bulb. I went to the window and I saw a man with an axe. He came to me and said here are the Chetniks coming towards us and I repeated that to my father. My father said hide yourself under the bed and that's what I did. Later on, the Chetniks came in and found us.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you remember, Witness, whether it was light or dark outside when you were looking out the window?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And what was it? Was it night-time? Was it daytime?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: It was daytime. It was still light.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when these men that you referred to as the Chetniks, when they arrived and they found you in the house, what did they do?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: We went outside. They ordered us to stand. They blindfolded us with white handkerchiefs, we boarded a green truck. My handkerchief fell off but another Chetnik put it back on and tied it very tightly.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, do you remember today how the Chetniks or what you refer to as the Chetniks were dressed that day?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And when you went on this green truck, do you have any recollection of where you were sitting?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Was your father with you on that truck?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you told us that your blindfold was slipping. Did that happen when you were outside or when you were on the truck?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: While I was on the truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And how did it come about that the Chetnik tightened your blindfold, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes, I can. We were on the truck. My father wanted to get up and put a kerchief on me. The Chetnik didn't allow him to do that. He went back to his seat and this Chetnik then approached me and tightened it very tight.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you went on a journey on this truck; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And did the truck at some point -- the truck that you were on, did it at some point come to a stop?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened after it came to a stop?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: We got off. They removed the white blindfolds. They ordered us to lie down on our stomachs and they started shooting at us.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you remember, Witness, what you saw when they removed your blindfold? How did the place look like?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: It was dark.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Were you taken somewhere -- was it inside? Was it outside? Were there trees? Were there no trees? Do you remember any of that?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: We got off, got out, and when they took off the blindfolds, I saw it was dark so nothing could be seen any longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, as you were lying -- when they ordered you to lie down, as you were lying down, do you remember anything specifically happening at that point in time? Maybe I can --

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It's okay. Do you remember telling us about a man who was -- that you saw running away and being shot. Do you remember anything about that?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: He got up and started running away. A Chetnik said, "Stop or I'll shoot." But he continued running. The Chetnik killed him. He fell down on to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And was it after that incident that the shooting began?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, do you remember feeling that you were injured during the shooting? Do you recall any of your sensations?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Would you like to share those with us?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Do you want me to show you or how do I do it? Shall I show you? Show you where I was wounded? Is that what you want me to do?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, you can tell us where you were wounded and then you can show us.

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Oh, all right. Do I need to stand up?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You can stand up, Witness.

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. We have to be very careful with the face distortion. So therefore, I suggest that we -- either you just tell us or otherwise we would have to go into closed session. If you just tell us that is good as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd rather show you. I can't describe it. It's much easier for me to demonstrate this to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now most likely for us to see it you will have to move a bit, so we go into closed session for a second. So if you have just some patience until the curtains are down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in closed session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Perhaps, Witness, if you stand and if you want to show us any scars or wounds, perhaps you take the place where the usher is now so that we can see it well. So you may stand up. Perhaps if you could keep your headphones on and take a position and perhaps a little bit coming forward so that the Defence can see it as well. Yes, if you would show where your woundings were.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This leg here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness is pointing at his left knee area. Was that the only place where you were wounded or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also in my arm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you indicate where in your arm you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness points at a position just above his right elbow at the back. Thank you very much for showing us. If you would take your seat again and then we return into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness, Ms. Hasan certainly will have more questions for you. Listen carefully to her.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, the injuries you just showed us, were those gunshot wounds?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you still have scars at those locations?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I understand that one scar is worse than the other. Can you -- are you able to describe the scar for us?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Well, I'll do my best, if I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You can go ahead if you want to describe it but just -- if you can just stay seated. If you can't describe it very well, that's okay.

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: It is a little bit difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, is this scar on your knee worse than the scar on your arm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the one on the leg is the worse. If you touch it, you can feel a sort of hole in the flesh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what size is that approximately. I'll try to point it out with my fingers, is it like this size or is it larger?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A bit smaller.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A bit smaller.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A distance of approximately one and a half centimetres with my fingers. I don't know whether we need further details on this, Ms. Hasan. If not, please proceed with any other question you may have.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And just to -- just one point of clarification. You also have a scar on your -- above your right elbow; that's correct?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, let's go back to when you were lying down. Can you tell us where your father was at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly. I don't know where he was. Anyway, he wasn't near me. He was farther away. We were not near each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, after the shooting had stopped, what happened? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: A white jeep approached us with the markings of the Red Cross, came up to the Chetniks, and asked them to let me go. They let me go. I went up close and I got into the white jeep. And that's where I started to bleed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you remember where you went in that jeep that you were in? Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: To the hospital. To the hospital in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: When you arrived, were you treated there for your injuries?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you remember what happened?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us a little bit about that?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can. I was lying down in the bath and I started to resist, shiver, I resisted and then I -- the doctors gave me something. They started to stitch my wounds. Then I was lying down in bed. There was a film and then it finished, and then there was some music and this music frightened me, so I went over there and asked them to turn it off.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you remember at all how long you stayed in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And after you were at the hospital, where did you go from there, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: I went somewhere. I asked who was going to take me and nobody wanted to take me in except my aunt and uncle. They took me in and I'm still living with them.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'm going to ask you a question and it's a difficult one. So if you can't answer it, that's fine. So what I'd like to ask you is if you can share with us how these events that you experienced have impacted your life today?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: It's a difficult question. I cannot answer this question. I'm sorry but I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's okay. I'm just going to ask you a few more questions about when you came here before and testified in another courtroom at this Tribunal. Okay?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you remember coming here in 2007 and you came here again in 2010. Do you remember those trips?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And do you recall the first time you gave -- you came here in 2007. Do you recall that we went through the evidence that you gave at that time just a few days ago, we did that?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And were the questions and answers read to you in a language that you understood?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Was there anything that was read to you that you want to correct today? Was there anything that was wrong?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can you put these questions to me one by one. Then it will be easier for me to answer. Can you do it the way you did earlier?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let's try it again. When the questions and answers were read to you in your language, do you remember whether any of the answers you had given were not true? Was everything that you had said, was it true?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. I didn't understand this before. It was difficult. This way I understand what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would on that basis offer the excerpt from the Popovic testimony into evidence under seal, it's 65 ter 28938.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections? Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28938 receives number P1535, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1535 is admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, thank you very much for answering my questions, and it's an honour for you to be in our presence today. And if you wouldn't mind if anyone else has questions for you right now, if you wouldn't mind answering those.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hasan. I have a small question for you. You said you didn't remember exactly how long you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't remember how long exactly you stayed in that hospital. Did you stay overnight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you stay there one night or even more nights?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was there for a few nights but I don't know how many. I don't remember that anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
