utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Now, Mr. Stojanovic who is seated -- well he's standing up now. Mr. Stojanovic may have some questions for you as well. Carefully listen to them and Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry to interrupt, I have just a couple of documents to offer from the bar and I'm more than happy to do it after the conclusion of this testimony if that's suitable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We would prefer to continue at this moment and then deal with that after. Mr. Stojanovic. You will find Mr. Stojanovic to your left. He's standing now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day.

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Good day to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to put a few questions to you. If you are tired or if you cannot answer, please feel free to tell me, but we are not going to take long. I quite understand the language that you speak and the language that I speak. So what I wanted to ask you was this, can you help me, can you tell me whether that place where you were loaded on to the truck was in the town of Srebrenica itself?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: No, no. It wasn't the town itself. It was just a house there. It was a village. It wasn't the town at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And are you able to recall the name of the village where you were when you were boarded on to the buses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, the witness said that he was in his house when the trucks arrived, so therefore if he answers that question, he might indicate where he was living. Now no one can hear you. Can you tell us where -- what village that was where you were picked up from that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you said it was not Srebrenica town --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said it was not Srebrenica town. Had -- that village, did it have a name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I don't remember. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it was close to Srebrenica town, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have any further questions where we should remain in private session, Mr. Stojanovic, tell us otherwise we'll return into open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suggest we move back into open session and we will be cautious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will return into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. You may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember how many people there were in the truck that you got into?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: There were many but I don't remember how many people there were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, would you please switch off your microphone while the witness is answering.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And are you able to tell me if you remember if it was an open or a closed truck that you were being driven in?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: It was open.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember how long they drove you in this truck?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Not long. It was a short ride. We got there quickly. It wasn't a long drive.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you try to orient us how long that was when you say that it wasn't long?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: No, I'm not able to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you recall whether you took an asphalt or a macadam road?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: No, it wasn't an asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you were told to get off the truck, was it still day?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: No, no, it was dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember if you stopped off anywhere on the way, at a school or at some other building?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: No. No, we didn't stop anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And are you able to remember whether at any point in time you noticed a railway track?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, that white vehicle with Red Cross markings, did you see when that arrived at the place where you were being shot at?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember perhaps how many people there were in that vehicle with the Red Cross markings?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to answer. Could you please repeat so it's a bit clearer? I didn't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I will try. We will take it slowly. Do you remember how many people there were in that white vehicle that had the Red Cross sign on it?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: You mean how many of us there were in the white jeep? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: It was just me and that doctor. No one else. I was sitting in the back and he was in the front. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The people who were shooting, do you remember them? Were they wearing uniforms or civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: I cannot remember them. I cannot remember that now. Before, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many of those people there were who were shooting?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: No. No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And this doctor who was with you in the white jeep, was he speaking in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You had a question from the Judges about how long -- about if you remember how long you stayed in the hospital and my colleague also asked you that.

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: I cannot remember. It was a few days. I was there for a while but I don't know how long.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And how did those doctors and the medical personnel treat you?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Well. It was fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember if they allowed you to go out and to play with other kids?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us if you remember how you were taken or driven to meet your family when you were taken from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would now like us to look at a document, 65 ter 05332, this is a document under seal so I would ask that it not be broadcast. 05332.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I am going to ask you to read it for yourself. Don't read it out loud. But do you see that your name is written anywhere on the document?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, again just read it to yourself where you can see in the upper right-hand corner where it says which village you come from. Please don't read it out loud but just tell us whether you recall even slightly the name of this village?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the place where you lived before you were brought?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And is that where you were staying at the point in time when you were boarded on to the truck and taken away?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at page 2 of this document and I repeat, this is a document under seal and it should not be broadcast outside of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to read a passage to you and I want to ask you something if you can remember it. In paragraph 2 here, it states that while you were staying with us, you adapted gradually. In the beginning was pretty nervous, did not communicate that much with other children. And then in time, he fit in and played with other children. Do you remember what I have just put to you now, that you did have the opportunity to play with other children?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This is quite confusing for him to confirm what's in this report. He's already said he doesn't recall the treatment, his treatment during his stay in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, apart from it's not very relevant, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to finish quickly with this document. I will do my best to be as specific as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whenever you refer to the document, you should adequately summarize if you want to put it to the witness and not use the language of the report itself which is official language. You should paraphrase as accurate as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to remember what the weather was like, what the season of the year was when you were taken from the hospital to your family?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document under seal in view of the contents of the document and also the note on the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 05332 receives number D304, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D304 is admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And I would just like to move into private session for the last few questions that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, just a couple more questions. Are you able to tell us if you remember who were you handed over to? Who waited for you when you were taken out of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: It was my aunt and uncle. They waited for me. Nobody else wanted to take me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell the Trial Chamber if you're working now?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: No, I'm not employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I will finish with this question. Can you please tell the Trial Chamber who are you living with now?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: With my aunt and uncle and my sister and my cousin.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know if your property was returned to you in the place where you were residing before the war?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you go back to your family property where you lived until the war?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you are living today where you lived before the war?

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, thank you. I am sorry if the testimony was upsetting, and I have no further questions for you. Witness, thank you for coming to testify.

utterances.speaker: RM313
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have the questions in cross-examination triggered any need for further examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness RM313, because that's how we call you here, this concludes your testimony. Yes, we still are in private session. We move first into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness RM313, this concludes your testimony in this courtroom and the Chamber but also the Prosecution and the Defence, we are all very glad that you came to answer all the questions we have although it may not have been easy for you. The more we appreciate that you came and we wish you a very safe journey home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you wait for a second, then the curtains will be down again and after that, you can move, you can follow the usher and he'll escort you out of the courtroom. We turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in closed session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will take a break after we have returned into open session. Is there any witness ready? Or you first would like to deal with some documents, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's deal with that then first.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I showed the witness a photograph in which he recognised himself in which is now P1534. Now, this photograph has been extracted from an ICRC notice looking for a family that would claim him. This is -- we can call it up. It's 65 ter 28009 and it should not be broadcast. Okay. So this is the document here, that is the photograph that I had shown him without any of the text, and we see his name recorded there, the name of his father, as well as other information including that he's presently at the Zvornik hospital. I'd like to offer this document from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28009 receives P1536, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's all. Then I repeat now my question whether the -- there is any Prosecution witness ready to follow after the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, the next Prosecution witness is ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll first take a break and resume at a quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President just while the witness is brought in, there was a transcript that we were using with the Petrovic video that we were watching. That transcript was not the most updated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, first of all you're not supposed to speak when someone else is speaking and second if you want to speak, you should do it at a lower volume. Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That transcript was not the updated version we have, in fact, there was a version that was worked on by the Prosecution in collaboration with Mr. Stojanovic and his team during the Popovic trial and that is the most recent one, so we've replaced the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you need the approval of the Chamber -- Madam Registrar needs the approval of the Chamber to replace anything in e-court, but we'll deal with that later. Let's first focus at this moment on -- good afternoon, Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. There is no need to repeat it but you are bound by it still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The examination-in-chief will now continue. Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes. Just to go back to that transcript because we will be using the new transcript during this part of the examination. The video and the road book -- sorry, the video itself was not MFI'd and hasn't been entered into evidence yet, so we did replace the transcript in e-court with a new one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. If it's not yet MFI'd or admitted, then you can still upload the version you wish in e-court. Now you want to tender them?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I can wait to do that at the end. I have a few corrections to references I made to the transcript before, but we can do that at the very end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The very end of testimony of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll wait for that. But we are now on notice that a new version has been uploaded. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd like to pull up now the transcript we've been talking about that's attached to 65 ter 24222.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I repeat: It's 24222.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently the --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I misspoke. It's 22422.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but whatever is the case, it seems that the computers are not yet -- there we are.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could have pages 10 in English and 11 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, if you remember, we were discussing a conversation that took place on the road via Motorola, and if we could actually -- the conversation begins on this page but let's turn to page 11 in English and the next page in the B/C/S. Witness, you see at the top of the page there we had previously discussed this conversation where we hear Ljubisa Borovcanin say Oficir, Bor, and you told us what those mean. I just want to get some clarification from you and that is the way that's being said there by Mr. Borovcanin, Oficir, Bor, that type of introduction, does that give us any clues as to who the conversation is between?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Here we see Ljubisa Borovcanin using the code-name or nickname of another officer, Oficir, in fact, calling him to the radio, and this is typical police conversation, not police, not only police but armed forces conversation through the radio handset -- radio, for example. If somebody calls somebody or just using his first whatever code-name or name, and introducing himself, he is using the short way to introducing himself. He called Oficir, Bor. It means Borovcanin calling Oficir and introducing himself as Bor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honour, if I may correct, he is talking -- this is -- translation here is "officer" but it was the exact word from B/C/S was translated because the name of this person, the proper name is Rade Cuturic and his nickname is "Oficir," and it was translated in this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you for that. If we could now play the Petrovic video where we left off. So that's 22422 and we pick up at 19 minutes, 10 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It appears we don't have any sound. If we could just pause it and ... Perhaps we can -- yeah, perhaps we can try again and see.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sorry, it's still very low, the sound. I can barely hear what's being said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can hear some voices in the background but the ramble is by far stronger than what we are supposed to hear. Is it the quality of the material or is it a technical problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can recall, the last time we played it in fact we heard it a little bit better than this. So I don't think it's the quality of the video itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: In fact, the questions I intend to ask don't relate to what's being said because it's only for the benefit of the Defence because we see what's being said here in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to play it again from the beginning, and if we have no sound, we still have the text. It's not complete then but if the Defence needs any additional explanation, then we'll hear from them. Could we restart where we started a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we just stop it right there? Perfect. And if we can -- sorry, that's at 21 minutes and 3 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, could you just remind us where we are along the road briefly?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are on the road Bratunac-Konjevic Polje. We are more or less in the location very near Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we could turn to the road book itself to the hard copies.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you have those before you at page 50 and 51. I believe that the Defence now has B/C/S versions of the road book in hard copy and that would assist now if we could give the witness also a copy of the road book.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. So we've almost stopped it here at the image we see on page 50 labelled video still B, and we see that we're about 100 metres from Sandici meadow. And, Witness, can you tell us is Mr. Borovcanin with Mr. Petrovic at this point in time when they've stopped here along the road?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Borovcanin is entire time with Zoran Petrovic, Pirocanac. I believe if we played that video, Mr. Borovcanin is visible here from -- on this picture a little bit behind the guy with blue helmet we see in the back -- in the back we see the car used also by Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Pirocanac. This is Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We will get to that image in just a few moments. Now, these persons we see in image A and B, can you tell us what units they're from if you know?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two person visible on this picture A and B, and they are members of the Jahorina unit. I believe they are members of the 1st Company of Jahorina unit commanded by Mane Djuric.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And we saw on the video that they're pointing their guns downwards, their rifles. Can you tell us what it is that they're aiming at or directing their rifles at?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below this road there is a stream going along the road, call it Krivace river, and this is quite few metres slope, and the people who are walking along the -- through the woods or through the hills on the right-hand side from, if you look at this picture here, they were -- were -- when they were surrendering to the Serb soldiers, they were going down to -- from the hill towards this direction towards the road and then taken to Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We see here in video still C on page 50 as well as the photograph number 3 on page 51, what have you tried to capture there?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to show on these two pictures that this is a creek or river just running along this road.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And can we in fact hear the river or creek on the video?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I believe we hear the creek on the video, but the river I don't know that is very well visible but it's possible to see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we didn't have very good sound on that. If we -- if there is a need later, we can go back to it but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we heard ramble rather than murmuring streams, yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. If we can continue then playing the video just for a few more seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we can pause it right there. That's at 21 minutes and 14 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, if we can turn now to page 52 and 53 now in our books. We almost have the image on our screens, that's on page 52, video still B. Can you tell us who the persons are that we see in that video still image.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we see Ljubisa Borovcanin with a soldier with blue helmet. It looks for me that this is soldier of special forces brigade because if you look at his left arm, it's visible at least partially, the badge of Special Police Brigade, and the man bending towards the open door of the car behind it, I believe this is Mr. Borovcanin driver, Nedjo -- his first name is Nedjo.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And if we just look at our screens, we in fact see another person there. Do you know who that is? A fourth person.

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are referring to, sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are referring, Ms. Hasan, I take it, to the person who is to the right of the person bending over looking into the car.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, the man who appears to be wearing a black T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us whether you know whose vehicle that is that we see there, the silver or white coloured vehicle?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is silver white colour vehicle. This is the vehicle used by Mr. Borovcanin and his driver and of course Mr. Pirocanac. According to the statement given to us by Mr. Borovcanin's driver, it is SEAT Toledo, and on the roof we see aerial also, the radio aerial.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, the man that you refer to wearing the blue helmet, does that helmet in fact belong to that unit or which force do the blue helmets belong to?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this type of helmet was never used by special police brigade at least in the Jahorina unit. That was used by UNPROFOR soldier. As I see here, it could be used by UNPROFOR. It could be UNPROFOR equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let's continue playing the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Just stop it right there. I'm sorry, if we could pause it right there. That's at 21 minutes and 59 seconds. And if we can turn to pages 54 and 55 in the road book.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, now we saw on the video and we see here on page 54 of your book men that appear to be walking. Can you tell us first where we are at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are in the back side of -- in fact -- yeah, on the left-hand side of this white destroyed house across the road of Sandici meadow, and these men, they are walking from the fields, and walking across -- they are passing this white destroyed house and they are passing the road. They are taken to Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: How is it that you have determined that they are in fact passing the destroyed white house?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you follow the movement of the camera, if you see the location over there, if you compare, for example, having this -- my picture from Petrovic video C from page 54, and let's say picture 1 and picture 2 from -- on page 55, you see that this is the house, this destroyed white house. Later on, we can see also -- also more details of this house.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get back to the house. And in photograph 3 that's on page 55 of your book, you have an arrow marked CAB. Is that the path that you've determined these men to have taken?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Here I marked by this arrow, I marked the path which was used by the men taken to Sandici meadow.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And have you taken that path yourself?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I was there so many times.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The hills in fact that we see behind the destroyed white house, for example, in photograph 1, are those the same hills that we earlier in the Petrovic video saw the Pragas shooting towards. Is that the same direction, the same right side of the road or is it another side?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is the same side of the road. This is the same hills.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And when you had referred to the men walking, coming from the hills, are those the hills you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. I'm referring to these hills behind this white destroyed house.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. We can continue playing the video, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could pause it right there, please. That's at 23 minutes and 8 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, if we turn the pages again in your book, pages 56 and 57, we see you've captured some of the images from that portion of the video clip. Now, can you tell us -- Witness, at the beginning of that clip we saw, and we see them a little bit in photo still image B, some uniformed persons. Can you tell us if you know who they are?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the still B from the page 56, we see the members of PJP unit. I do not recall their names now, but I'm sure that they are members of PJP. They have been recognised by us and they were interviewed by OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And in terms of figuring out the path that they took which you appear to have marked on page 57 in your photograph, can you tell us what you used to determine that path, what features?

utterances.speaker: TOMASZ BLASZCZYK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Location of this white destroyed house, shape of the road, the path, shape of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And if you can just assist us a little bit. On the video still images you've captured --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, I'm looking at the clock, it's quarter past 2.00. I think we should continue tomorrow. Mr. Blaszczyk, we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom I, and I again instruct you that should not speak with anyone about your testimony whether testimony already given or testimony still to be given.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow, Friday, the 7th of June at 9.30 in the morning in this same courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
